meta.titre: Word Families: building words from a root and finding opposites
meta.sous_theme: Roots, prefixes, suffixes and antonyms for vocabulary questions

sections.contenu_markdown: A child falls on a football pitch in Garoua and a teacher shouts: « Il saigne ! » (He is bleeding!). Someone brings a bandage, and the nurse writes about the *saignement* and the *sang*. These words belong to the same family: they are built on the same root. In Paper 1 of the GCE O Level French, a gap may need the noun, the verb or the adjective of a family, and another question may ask for the opposite of a word. Knowing how French builds words lets you answer both kinds quickly.

items: A noun names a person or a thing and usually follows an article (le, la, un).
A verb is conjugated; an adjective describes a noun and agrees with it.
A prefix is added before a word and a suffix after it.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What a word family is

A word family is a group of words built from the same root. Knowing the family helps you choose the right form for a gap (noun, verb, adjective or adverb) and find an opposite.

| Root idea | Noun | Verb | Adjective |
|---|---|---|---|
| warm | la chaleur | chauffer | chaud |
| cold | le froid | refroidir | froid |
| strength | la force | fortifier | fort |
| courage | le courage | encourager | courageux |

### Building words with suffixes

| Suffix | What it builds | Example |
|---|---|---|
| -eur / -euse | the person who does the action | vendre: vendeur, vendeuse |
| -ment | a noun from a verb | loger: le logement |
| -tion | a noun from a verb | informer: l'information |
| -age | a noun from a verb | nettoyer: le nettoyage |
| -eux / -euse | an adjective from a noun | le danger: dangereux |
| -té | a noun from an adjective | libre: la liberté |
| -ment | an adverb from an adjective | lent: lentement |

Adverbs in *-ment* are made from the feminine form (*lente*, *heureuse*): *lentement*, *heureusement*. Adjectives in *-ent* and *-ant* give *-emment* and *-amment*: *évident, évidemment; constant, constamment*.

### Opposites (antonyms)

Many opposites are made by adding a prefix.

| Prefix | Example pairs |
|---|---|
| in- | connu / inconnu, utile / inutile, juste / injuste |
| im- (before b, m, p) | possible / impossible, poli / impoli, patient / impatient |
| il- (before l) | légal / illégal, lisible / illisible |
| ir- (before r) | régulier / irrégulier, réel / irréel |
| dé- / dés- | faire / défaire, couvrir / découvrir, obéir / désobéir |
| mal- | heureux / malheureux, honnête / malhonnête, adroit / maladroit |
| mé- | content / mécontent |

The prefix cannot be guessed: the opposite of *heureux* is *malheureux*, not *inheureux*. Many words have an unrelated opposite: *grand / petit*, *riche / pauvre*, *ouvrir / fermer*, *monter / descendre*, *léger / lourd*. The opposite must keep the form of the word: same gender and number, same tense and person.

variantes.nom: Choosing the right member of the family in a gap
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the four options are forms of the same root and only one fits the sentence
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Decide the kind of word needed from the words around the gap.

| Clue | Word needed | Example |
|---|---|---|
| article or possessive before the gap (le, une, mon, leur) | noun | Mon oncle est un bon **travailleur**. |
| subject pronoun before the gap | conjugated verb | Ils **travaillent** dur. |
| *être*, *très* or a noun before the gap | adjective | Cette élève est très **travailleuse**. |
| a verb before the gap, describing how it is done | adverb in *-ment* | Elle parle **lentement**. |

Then check gender, number and the tense.

variantes.nom: Finding the opposite of an underlined word
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the instruction says Trouvez le contraire du mot souligné
variantes.contenu_markdown:
1. Say what kind of word it is: adjective, verb, noun or adverb.
2. Try a natural prefix (*in-*, *im-*, *il-*, *ir-*, *dé-*, *mal-*, *mé-*) and check that the result is a real French word.
3. If no prefix works, use a word of opposite meaning (*grand / petit*).
4. Give the answer in the same form: *Ces règles sont justes* becomes *Ces règles sont injustes*, with the plural *s*.
5. Reread the sentence to check that the meaning is the real opposite.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Choose the word that fills the gap: « Les voisins ont aidé la famille, qui les remercie de leur ____. »

(a) aider (b) aide (c) aidé (d) aidant

etapes.justification: All four options come from the same root, so the difference is in the form.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) infinitive, (b) noun, (c) past participle, (d) present participle.

etapes.action: Look at the word before the gap.
etapes.justification: *Leur* is a possessive determiner and is always followed by a noun.
An infinitive, a past participle and a present participle are verb forms and cannot follow a possessive determiner.

etapes.action: Check with the verb of the clause.
etapes.justification: *Remercier de* is followed by a noun: you thank someone for something.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *...qui les remercie de leur aide.* (...who thanks them for their help.)

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **(b) aide**. Choosing the right member of a family depends on the clue next to the gap: a possessive or an article points to a noun, a subject pronoun to a conjugated verb, *être* or *très* to an adjective.

items.pourquoi_faux: The prefix *in-* cannot be added to every word. The usual prefix for this word is *mal-*.
Before the letters b, m and p, the prefix *in-* becomes *im-*.

items.erreur_markdown: Opposite of « Les filles sont <u>contentes</u> » written as *Les filles sont mécontent.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: The opposite must keep the form of the original word. *Filles* is feminine plural, so the adjective must take *e* and *s*.
The word describes the verb *parle*, so an adverb is needed, not the adjective *lent*.
*Courage* is a noun. After *un homme* an adjective is needed.
items.correction_markdown: *C'est un homme **courageux**.* (He is a courageous man.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Give the opposite of each word by adding a prefix.

(a) utile

(b) possible

(c) heureux

(d) obéir
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **inutile**. *In-* before a vowel sound.

(b) **impossible**. *Im-* before *p*.

(c) **malheureux**. The prefix *mal-* is used with this word.

(d) **désobéir**. *Dés-* before a vowel.

items.enonce_markdown:
Choose the right word of the family to fill each gap.

(a) Le pompier est très ____. (courageux / courage / encourager)

(b) Il fait une grande ____ aujourd'hui. (chaleur / chaud / chauffer)

(c) Maman va ____ l'eau pour le thé. (chaleur / chaud / chauffer)

(d) Cette élève est très ____. (travail / travailler / travailleuse)
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **courageux**. *Très* is followed by an adjective: *Le pompier est très courageux.* (The fireman is very brave.)

(b) **chaleur**. *Une grande* is followed by a noun: *Il fait une grande chaleur aujourd'hui.* (It is very hot today.)

(c) **chauffer**. After *va* an infinitive is needed: *Maman va chauffer l'eau pour le thé.* (Mum is going to heat the water for tea.)

(d) **travailleuse**. After *très* an adjective, feminine because of *élève*: *Cette élève est très travailleuse.* (This pupil is very hardworking.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Give the opposite of each underlined word, keeping the right form.

(a) Ces règles sont <u>justes</u>.

(b) Il a <u>fermé</u> la porte.

(c) Les voisins sont <u>polis</u>.

(d) Elle a <u>couvert</u> la casserole.

(e) Cette valise est <u>légère</u>.

(f) Explain why the opposite of *adroit* can be built with a prefix but the opposite of *grand* cannot.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **injustes**. In- + justes, plural.

(b) **ouvert**. No prefix works, so a word of opposite meaning is used: *Il a ouvert la porte.*

(c) **impolis**. Im- before *p*, plural.

(d) **découvert**. Dé- + couvert: *Elle a découvert la casserole.*

(e) **lourde**. *Légère* is feminine singular, so the opposite is *lourde*: *Cette valise est lourde.*

(f) *Adroit* has the opposite *maladroit*, made with the prefix *mal-*. *Grand* has an opposite of unrelated form, *petit*, which cannot be built with a prefix. A prefix works only with some words, so you must learn which words form opposites with a prefix.

items_markdown: A word family is a group of words built on the same root: noun, verb, adjective and adverb forms (chaud, chaleur, chauffer).
Suffixes build words: *-eur/-euse* (doer), *-ment, -tion, -age* (nouns from verbs), *-eux* (adjectives), *-té* (nouns from adjectives), *-ment* (adverbs).
Opposites are often made with a prefix: *in-, im-, il-, ir-, dé-/dés-, mal-, mé-*. Use *im-* before b, m, p; *il-* before l; *ir-* before r.
Some opposites have a different word: grand / petit, riche / pauvre, ouvrir / fermer. Do not force a prefix.
In a gap-fill question, read the words around the gap (article, possessive, subject pronoun, *être*, *très*) to know whether you need a noun, a verb, an adjective or an adverb.
The opposite must keep the form of the original word: same gender and number, same tense and person.
